keep taking care of yourself. keep doing what makes you feel good. the noise gets a lot quieter when you’re proud of the woman you’re becoming.🫶

meanwhile crush up 1/2 cup of farm girl cinnamon crisps. mix together blended cottage cheese mixture, cinnamon crisps and 1/2 cup of chopped strawberries. 

put in the freezer for a couple of hours until firm and enjoy!🍓🍰🤎

caption:
one thing that made eating more protein feel way less overwhelming was learning the “add a zero” trick.💪💕

how it works:

take the grams of protein in a food and add a zero to the end.

17g protein → 170

compare that number to the calories.

if the calories are lower than (or close to) that number, it’s usually a pretty protein-dense option.

for example:

✔️ greek yogurt
17g protein
90 calories
17 → 170
90 calories is well under that, making it a great protein source.

the biggest thing this helped me with was quickly spotting foods that would actually help me stay full and hit my protein goals.

it’s not a perfect rule, and there are lots of nutritious foods that won’t pass the test, but as a quick grocery-store shortcut? it’s been surprisingly helpful.

save this for your next grocery run.🛒💨

High-protein, comforting, and made with delicious Cosmic Crisp® apples from @washingtonapples.canada. This Cozy High-Protein Apple Crisp Bowl recipe creates 4 servings. 

INGREDIENTS:

APPLE BASE
• 4 Washington Apples - Cosmic Crisp® apples, chopped
 • 4 tsp cinnamon (or to taste)
 • 4 tsp maple syrup
 • ¼ cup water

CRISP TOPPING
• ½ cup oats
 • ¼ cup almond butter
 • 2–3 tsp cinnamon

PROTEIN BASE
• 2½–3 cups plain Greek yogurt
 • Optional: 1 scoop vanilla protein powder stirred into yogurt

INSTRUCTIONS:
Add chopped Cosmic Crisp® apples, cinnamon, maple syrup, and water to a large pan.

Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until soft.

In a separate pan, toast oats with almond butter and cinnamon until golden.

Divide yogurt into 4 bowls.

Top with warm apples and crisp topping.

Finish with extra cinnamon.

caption:
I used to rush through my evenings, trying to squeeze in everything once the kids went to bed. And somehow, I’d still go to sleep feeling wired instead of rested.

So I started making small changes. Nothing dramatic. Just little habits that helped my nervous system slow down.

1. I dim the lights as soon as it starts getting dark, it’s my cue that the day is winding down. 

2. I said goodbye to worn out pjs and started wearing a matching set each night. It’s something I look forward to each evening because feeling comfortable and put together shifts my whole mood (even when it’s just to go to sleep).

3. My mom used to always remind my grandma in the evenings to do her skincare and put on her favourite scent (either a light perfume or soft scented lotion). I love this luxury, making my nighttime routine feel a bit more lux.

4. I reset the kitchen and run the dishwasher so I don’t wake up to yesterday’s mess. It makes such a difference in my mood in the morning. 

5. I end the night with a cup of spearmint tea. A small, calming ritual that tells my body it’s okay to rest.

These aren’t big luxuries. They’re just small ways I care for myself in this busy season of life.🫶

#momlife #millenialmom #nighttimeroutine #skincareroutine #dailyhabit
